Subject: POC extension / top-up question

Hey Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited. We’re mid-way through the 30-day time-boxed POC and seeing a higher-than-expected burst profile during model evaluation (interactive sessions + nightly batch runs). We have two asks:

1) Is there a straightforward way to add a short top-up so we don’t hit limits before the official close?
2) If we convert to a committed package within 60–90 days, how do you credit any unused trial allocation (if at all)? Do you do prorated credit or convert the remaining hours into a discounted commit?

We prefer minimal paperwork if possible — a short amendment or an invoice for additional units would be fine. Attaching the quick usage CSV from our side for reference (saffron-poc-usage.csv).

CC'ing Carlos (Procurement) for timeline visibility.

Thanks,
Maya

Saffron AI

Hi Maya — really glad to hear the team is getting value. Short answers up front: yes, and yes (with options). Details below so you can pick the path that best fits how your procurement team wants to move.

Option A — Hour-pool top-up (fast, low-friction)
- One-off add of N GPU-hours applied to your existing POC allocation.
- Immediate consumption; billing as a single invoice.
- No automatic conversion credits. If you convert to a commit, we can offer a one-time conversion credit equal to 30% of the top-up amount if conversion happens within 30 days of top-up.

Option B — Flexible credit bucket (recommended for bursty tests)
- Buy a credit bucket (tokens) that draws down for both interactive and batch usage.
- Upfront payment, valid for 90 days.
- If you convert to a monthly committed plan within 90 days, remaining credits convert to committed usage at a 1:1 rate plus a 10% bonus credit applied on top (i.e., leftover 100 credits become 110 committed credits).

Operational notes:
- We can do Option A same-day with a short email amendment. Option B needs a 1-page amendment (we can draft).
- I attached a quick estimate based on your CSV and a couple of burst scenarios.

Next steps suggestion: tell me which option you prefer and the rough budget number; I’ll loop in Laura on the amendment and get a one-pager over for sign-off.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
